profile.reading:
This building sits on Statesboro Place in Brambleton, Loudoun County, Virginia, in the same broader Stone Ridge/Brambleton corridor where Bisnow reported Microsoft built its 500,000-square-foot "IAD11" data center on nearby Growth Mindset Lane in the Arcola Business Park for roughly $400 million. Microsoft's Brambleton-area presence is part of a wider Northern Virginia footprint that Bisnow's reporting described as spanning Ashburn, Leesburg, Sterling, Manassas City, and Prince William County in addition to Loudoun County. Loudoun County's own economic development office has said data centers contributed $859 million in county tax revenue in 2025, with computer equipment personal property tax from data centers, about $670.3 million in fiscal year 2025, the county's single largest personal property tax revenue source; Microsoft is among the county's largest data center taxpayers alongside Amazon Web Services and Google. Microsoft has also invested directly in Loudoun County community programs, including STEM kits for Loudoun Public Schools middle school students distributed through the Loudoun Education Foundation. Microsoft has not published this specific Statesboro Place building's investment figure, square footage, MW capacity, or relationship to the nearby IAD11 project, so this registry records the Brambleton-area IAD11 figures and county-wide tax data as regional context rather than facts confirmed for this exact structure.

Dominion Energy, the regional utility serving Loudoun and Prince William counties, has repeatedly cited Northern Virginia data center growth as the largest driver of new electricity demand in its Virginia service territory in filings with the Virginia State Corporation Commission, prompting new transmission and generation investment; Virginia's data center sales-and-use tax exemption, administered by the Virginia Economic Development Partnership, has been a material factor cited by state and local officials in why Microsoft and other hyperscalers have concentrated so much investment in this specific corridor rather than spreading it across lower-tax states.

reading.body:
Microsoft does not publish exact capacity figures for individual Azure data center campuses, including this Loudoun County site. The operator discloses only aggregate worldwide statistics: 500+ datacenters across 80+ regions, 40+ gigawatts of renewable energy contracted globally, and 800,000+ kilometers of network fiber. Without a published megawatt figure for this specific campus, its size relative to the broader Azure infrastructure cannot be determined from official sources.

Virginia hosts 326 mapped data center facilities, of which only 23 operators have published power capacity. Those 23 facilities account for 1,375 MW of disclosed capacity across the state. This Microsoft campus in Loudoun County sits within Northern Virginia's Data Center Alley alongside major AWS, Google, and Meta facilities, but ranks 24th among Virginia sites with published figures, meaning at least one other facility in the state has disclosed more capacity. The published capacity figure for this campus is not available.

Whether this campus matters to AI scaling cannot be assessed from published data. Microsoft's decision to withhold individual campus capacity figures, combined with the broader operator trend of minimal disclosure, leaves the site's contribution to national AI infrastructure compute growth unmeasurable from public sources. Grid impact, rack density, and actual utilization remain unknown.
